card: This PR verifies the hardcoded AssumeUTXO snapshot hash during standard Initial Block Download when block connection reaches the commitment height, triggering a fatal error and node shutdown on a mismatch. Full nodes independently rebuild the UTXO set from genesis during IBD, but previously never checked whether their reconstructed UTXO set matched the baked-in commitments (#32377). To avoid multiple expensive UTXO hashing passes during IBD, chainparams is changed to retain only the single latest AssumeUTXO commitment per network, retiring support for loading older snapshots.
changed_since_previous: Propagates snapshot verification errors out of ConnectTip as runtime errors instead of reporting success, and refines interruption handling so interrupted hashing during shutdown is not recorded as a validation failure.
evidence: Linked issue #32377 ('AssumeUTXO: crowdsource trust through independent snapshot verification') notes that every syncing full node could automatically audit hardcoded snapshot hashes during standard IBD.
Commit 36a2a70452 explains: 'This checks the developer-provided commitment against the UTXO set that every node reconstructs during IBD (see #32377).'
problem: AssumeUTXO relies on hardcoded snapshot hashes compiled into the node binary. Even though nodes running standard IBD independently reconstruct the exact UTXO set from genesis, they never compare it against the hardcoded commitment, passing up crowd-sourced verification of baked-in snapshot commitments against history (#32377).

risk.why: It inserts a synchronous disk flush, multi-minute UTXO hashing pass, and potential fatal error exit into ConnectTip during normal block validation.

scope_notes: Retaining only the single latest snapshot commitment is a breaking change for loading older AssumeUTXO snapshots or restarting snapshot chainstates built against retired commitments.
summary: Verifies the hardcoded AssumeUTXO commitment during normal Initial Block Download when block connection reaches the snapshot height and block hash. Pending UTXO modifications are synchronously flushed to disk, the serialized UTXO set is hashed, and a mismatch or failure causes the node to shut down with a fatal error. To prevent repeated multi-minute hashing passes during IBD, chainparams is simplified to store only the single most recent AssumeUTXO commitment per network, deprecating older snapshot activations.
